note: Philosophy note of the day: serious philosophy, read closely. One passage a day from a major philosopher, quoted exactly from a named edition or translation, with a gloss that states the argument, its place in the work and the strongest objection. No aphorism collections, no self-help, no quotation sites. The run appends {date, thinker, work, tradition} here so no thinker repeats within 30 days and no work within 90; `canon` is the pool to draw from and may grow with thinkers of the same weight.
traditions: Medieval and early modern (Augustine, Aquinas, Spinoza, Hobbes, Locke)
German idealism and its critics (Hegel, Schopenhauer, Marx)
Existentialism (Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Heidegger, Sartre, Camus, de Beauvoir)
Political thought (Arendt, Machiavelli, Berlin, Rawls, Schmitt read critically)
Phenomenology and hermeneutics (Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, Gadamer, Levinas)
Philosophy of war and violence (Clausewitz, Walzer, Weil, Arendt on violence)
Non-Western (Confucius, Zhuangzi, Nagarjuna, al-Farabi, Ibn Khaldun)
